title: FRET‐FLIM to Determine Protein Interactions and Membrane Topology of Enzyme Complexes
author: Spatola Rossi, Pain, et al.

CAUTION: The detectors for FLIM are extremely sensitive, and care must be taken not to expose them to too much light. The use of a remote light switch minimizes the user's movements in the darkened room.

steps.title: Prepare YEB growth medium
steps.instruction: Combine 5 g L⁻¹ beef extract, 1 g L⁻¹ yeast extract, 5 g L⁻¹ sucrose and 0.5 g L⁻¹ MgSO₄·7H₂O in deionized water, autoclave, and store at room temperature for up to 12 months.

steps.title: Prepare infiltration buffer
steps.instruction: Make fresh buffer the day before use containing 50 mM MES, 2 mM Na₃PO₄·12H₂O, 0.1 mM acetosyringone and 5 g L⁻¹ glucose in deionized water; prepare MES and Na₃PO₄ stocks and keep at 4 °C for ≤1 month, store acetosyringone stock at –20 °C for ≤12 months; filter‑sterilization not required.

steps.title: Grow Agrobacterium cultures
steps.instruction: Inoculate Agrobacterium transformed with the fluorescent‑protein constructs into YEB medium with appropriate antibiotics, incubate in 15‑mL conical tubes at 28 °C shaking incubator overnight.

substeps.instruction: Use 2‑mL microcentrifuge tubes with safe‑lock for aliquoting.
Measure culture density with a microvolume spectrophotometer (e.g., NanoDrop 2000).

steps.title: Resuspend Agrobacterium to desired OD
steps.instruction: Centrifuge overnight cultures, discard supernatant, and resuspend the pellet in infiltration buffer to an OD₆₀₀ of 0.1 (starting point for expression optimization).

substeps.instruction: If needed, adjust OD by adding more buffer or concentrating the pellet.
Keep the suspension on ice until infiltration.

steps.title: Infiltrate tobacco leaves
steps.instruction: Using a sterile 1‑mL syringe without needle, gently press the Agrobacterium suspension into the abaxial side of 4‑ to 6‑week‑old Nicotiana tabacum or N. benthamiana leaves until the leaf area is uniformly infiltrated.

substeps.instruction: Work on several leaves per plant to obtain enough tissue for later imaging.

steps.title: Incubate infiltrated plants
steps.instruction: Place infiltrated plants in a standard plant growth chamber under normal tobacco growth conditions and incubate for 48–72 h (optimal visualization at 72 h) to allow transient protein expression.

substeps.instruction: Water plants as needed; no further manipulation required.

steps.title: Mount leaf section for imaging
steps.instruction: Excise a ~5 mm² leaf piece expressing the fluorescent proteins, place it on a microscope slide, add enough water to keep it hydrated, cover with a coverslip, and secure with surgical tape.

steps.title: Darken laboratory for FLIM
steps.instruction: Turn off all laboratory lights using the remote‑controlled switch (keep only emergency lighting and luminescent safety strips on) to protect the sensitive FLIM detectors.

steps.title: Configure microscope for FRET‑FLIM
steps.instruction: Set up the two‑channel confocal / FLIM system (e.g., Nikon TE2000‑U with modified EC2 scanner) with a mode‑locked Ti:Sapphire laser (e.g., Coherent Mira) and a 532‑nm CW laser (e.g., Coherent Verdi V18), high‑NA objective (e.g., Nikon VC series), BG39 filter, 633‑nm interference filter, and TCSPC card (e.g., Becker & Hickl SPC 830 or SPC150). Load FLIM image analysis software (e.g., SPCImage NG v5.1 or later).

steps.title: Locate and focus leaf cells
steps.instruction: Using the eyepiece and white light, bring the infiltrated leaf cells into focus on the slide before engaging the laser scanning system.

steps.title: Acquire FLIM images
steps.instruction: Activate the laser scanning system, confirm protein expression, then collect FLIM data with the pulsed laser; set acquisition time between ~10 s and 120 s depending on sample brightness, using the TCSPC device to record photon arrival times at MHz pixel dwell rates.

substeps.instruction: For each donor‑acceptor combination acquire 10 cells from at least two different plants (n = 2).
With practice, generate 50–75 FLIM images per day (≈3 donor‑acceptor pairs plus controls).

steps.title: Collect control datasets
steps.instruction: Record FLIM lifetimes for donor‑only samples and for donor plus a non‑interacting acceptor to provide statistical baselines for interaction analysis.

steps.title: Analyze lifetime data
steps.instruction: Using the FLIM analysis software, calculate fluorescence lifetimes for each region of interest, then compute average and standard deviation across biological and technical replicates; a lifetime reduction ≥0.2 ns indicates FRET. Perform statistical comparison (e.g., Kruskal‑Wallis test) between donor‑only and donor‑acceptor samples.

substeps.instruction: Present results as bar graphs or tables as appropriate.

steps.title: Optional: Apply latrunculin B
steps.instruction: If ER mobility limits acquisition, treat leaf discs with latrunculin B (as described in literature) to depolymerize actin and stabilize ER cisternae before imaging.
